title: Two People Die in Fire at Food Kiosk Within Mombasa Port
desc: Two people have died and two others were taken to hospital after a fire broke out at a food kiosk within Kenya Ports Authority premises in Mombasa
content:
Two people have died following a fire at a food kiosk within the Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) premises in Mombasa, with two others taken to hospital as police investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Mombasa County Police Commander Stella Cherono confirmed the fatalities on Monday, November 23, 2026, saying the fire broke out at a kiosk within the port authority's premises.

According to the police commander, preliminary information suggests that a gas cylinder may have been involved. However, investigators are yet to establish the exact cause of the fire.

Cherono said two people lost their lives while two others were rushed to Coast General Hospital for treatment.

Emergency Teams Contain the Fire

Fire response teams from the Kenya Ports Authority and the Mombasa County Government responded to the incident and managed to contain the fire before it spread to neighbouring buildings.

The police commander said the affected area had been secured and was considered safe, as investigations continued to establish what happened.

The response helped prevent the blaze from spreading further within the premises, although the incident resulted in loss of life and injuries.

Cause of Fire Still Under Investigation

Police have not established whether a gas cylinder explosion or another gas-related incident triggered the fire. The suspected involvement of a gas cylinder remains a preliminary assessment rather than a confirmed finding.

Investigations will be important in establishing how the fire started and the circumstances that led to the deaths and injuries.

The incident also draws attention to the importance of fire preparedness and safe handling of cooking equipment in busy workplace food outlets.

Further information, including the identities of those who died and the condition of the injured, had not been confirmed in the initial police account.
